In Manufacturing & Industrial, data, analytics & lakehouse is the substrate tower: pipeline modernization, lakehouse architecture on databricks and snowflake, streaming and event-driven decisioning, executive bi, master data and cataloging, predictive analytics, and data products that generate revenue. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: data engineering & pipeline modernization, lakehouse architecture & migration, real-time streaming & event-driven decisioning — delivered on Dataq Forge and Dataq Nexus with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: MES/ERP/quality data silos
Process telemetry, quality records and ERP lots never meet; root-cause analysis takes weeks of manual correlation when a customer complaint arrives.
Brownfield instrumentation gap
Critical assets run uninstrumented because gut-and-replace is unthinkable; the data that twins and models need does not exist, and downtime for retrofit is unaffordable.
Quality escapes and manual inspection

Defect detection depends on sampling and eyes; escapes reach customers, and scrap/rework costs hide in the P&L. Vision systems stall in pilot because lighting, thresholds and line integration were never engineered.

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: ESG reporting (CSRD/ISSB) and ISO 9001/IATF 16949 quality systems. Traceability and process control evidence for audits. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

Below is the delivery cadence for this capability — the same pattern on every engagement. The first quarter of the rhythm is verification: weeks 1–2 measure the current metric with your team and lock it by signature. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with your control owner receiving evidence weekly. Weeks 9–12 industrialize: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and the measured delta against the signed baseline. Gates are binding: miss one and the program stops or redirects with a documented decision.
